Purpose: Sets out how the company protects the information it holds and the service it provides, who is responsible, and how the policy set is managed.
Scope: All staff, contractors and systems in the system boundary.
Brain fields to draw on: Team Details, Governance, Operating Cadence, Company Stage, Framework Scope, Control execution
Ask the client: Who signs off policies? Which leadership meeting already happens where security could be a standing item? Who do staff go to with a security question?

Purpose: Sets out how staff may use company systems, devices, data and AI tools.
Scope: All staff and contractors with access to company systems or data.
Brain fields to draw on: Workspace, Endpoint model, Workforce model, AI Models and Platforms, Data Handled
Ask the client: Can staff use personal devices or personal AI accounts for work? Which AI tools are approved? How do new starters accept policies today?

Purpose: Sets the behaviour expected of staff, including integrity, confidentiality and reporting misconduct, and the consequences of breaches.
Ask the client: Do you already have a code of conduct or employee handbook? Who handles disciplinary matters?

Purpose: Covers security across the employee lifecycle: hiring, onboarding, training, role changes and leaving.
Scope: Employees and contractors with access to company systems or data.
Brain fields to draw on: Headcount, HR System, Workforce model, Country/Region(s), Identity and Authentication, Device Management, Password Manager
Ask the client: Who runs onboarding, and what's on the checklist? When someone leaves, who tells IT and how quickly is access removed? Do contractors go through the same steps? How is security training done today?

Purpose: Sets out how access to systems and data is requested, approved, reviewed and removed.
Scope: All systems in the system boundary, including production, the identity provider, workspace and code repository.
Brain fields to draw on: Access ownership, Privileged & production access, Provider access to customer data, Customer administration, Identity and Authentication, Password Manager, Privileged Access Management
Ask the client: Who approves access for a new starter, and where is that recorded? Who has admin access to production today? When do your people look at customer data, and who allows it?

Purpose: Sets out how the company identifies, rates, treats and monitors risks to its service and commitments, including fraud.
Scope: Risks to the in-scope system, the company and its customers.
Brain fields to draw on: Risk management, Operating Cadence, Planned Changes, Known Gaps, Compliance Goals
Ask the client: Who decides when a risk is acceptable? When does leadership already review priorities, where a risk review could fit? What worries you most that could go wrong?

Purpose: Sets out how vendors are selected, assessed, contracted and reviewed, based on the data and services they provide.
Scope: All third parties that provide services, hold company or customer data, or have access to company systems.
Brain fields to draw on: Vendor management, Subservice Providers, Infrastructure, Hosting Platform, AI Models and Platforms
Ask the client: Who can sign up for a new tool, and does anyone check it first? Who pays the bills and keeps the contracts? Which vendors would hurt most if they went down?

Purpose: Sets out how information is classified, handled, encrypted, retained and deleted.
Scope: All company and customer data in the system boundary, in any format.
Brain fields to draw on: Data Handled, Data minimisation, Data control boundary, Tenancy & isolation, Databases, Application Secrets and Encryption, Service Commitments
Ask the client: What customer data do you hold, and where? How long do you keep it after a customer leaves? Do you ever copy production data into test?

Purpose: Sets out how devices and other assets are tracked, secured and disposed of, and how physical sites are protected.
Scope: Company-owned and personal devices used for work, and any offices or equipment in scope.
Brain fields to draw on: Device Management, Endpoint Protection, Endpoint model, Facilities, Workforce model
Ask the client: Who sets up laptops for new starters? What happens to a laptop when someone leaves? Is there an office with anything sensitive in it?

Purpose: Sets out how infrastructure is secured, monitored and kept free of known vulnerabilities.
Scope: Production infrastructure, cloud accounts, networks and the tools that monitor them.
Brain fields to draw on: Infrastructure, Hosting Platform, Infrastructure operations, Edge and Web Protection, Infrastructure Vulnerability Scanning, Software Vulnerability Scanning, Audit Logging, Security Threat Detection, Penetration Test Status
Ask the client: Who gets alerted if something looks wrong in production, and at what hours? How do you find out about vulnerabilities today? When was your last pen test?

Policy: Secure Development and Change Management Policy
Purpose: Sets out how changes to code, infrastructure and configuration are designed, reviewed, tested and released.
Scope: Application code, infrastructure, configuration and data changes to the in-scope system.
Brain fields to draw on: Change management, Release Frequency, Code Repository, Build and Deployment / CI/CD, Infrastructure Configuration, Ticketing, Service standardisation
Ask the client: Walk me through how a change gets to production. Can anyone deploy on their own? What happens when something urgent needs fixing at night?

Purpose: Sets out how security incidents are reported, handled, communicated and learned from.
Scope: Security and availability incidents affecting the in-scope system, company data or customer data.
Brain fields to draw on: Incident response, Service Commitments, Regulatory Drivers, Country/Region(s), Customer Geography, Status Page
Ask the client: If you had a security incident tonight, who would lead it? Who decides whether to tell customers? How quickly have you promised to notify customers of a breach?

Policy: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy
Purpose: Sets out how the company keeps the service running and recovers data and systems after a disruption.
Scope: The in-scope service, its data, and the people and vendors it depends on.
Linked controls: BC-01A, BC-01B, BC-02, AV-01A, AV-01B, AV-02, AV-03, AV-04A, AV-04B, AV-05A, AV-05B, AV-06, AV-07A, AV-07B, AV-09
Brain fields to draw on: Backups and Recovery, Availability responsibility, Service Commitments, Hosting Platform, Auto-scaling, Availability Monitoring, Status Page
Ask the client: If your main cloud region went down, what would you do? How much data could you afford to lose? Have you ever restored from a backup?

Purpose: Sets out how personal information is collected, used, shared, kept and protected, and how individuals' rights are handled.
Scope: Personal information the company collects or processes about customers, their users and staff.
Brain fields to draw on: Data Handled, Regulatory Drivers, Customer Geography, Country/Region(s), Privacy Policy, Data minimisation
Ask the client: Who handles privacy requests from customers or individuals? Does personal data go overseas? Who would deal with a privacy complaint?

Purpose: Sets out how AI tools, AI features and AI agents are approved, used, tested and monitored.
Scope: AI tools used by staff, AI features in the product, and AI agents acting for the company.
Brain fields to draw on: AI Models and Platforms, AI reliance, Responsibility for outcomes, Control execution, Data Handled
Ask the client: Which AI tools does the team use day to day? Does the product use AI, and who checks its output? Do any agents take actions on their own?
